scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY-Inland): Establishment of Medium RAS Culture System Gujarat
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on September 10, 2020. 

This scheme aims to bring about a significant transformation in the fisheries sector. 

The PMMSY is designed to enhance fish production and productivity. 

It also aims to promote the welfare of fishers and fish farmers. 

The scheme has a special focus on sustainable development. 

The PMMSY has an overall outlay of ₹20,050 crores. 

This outlay is spread over a period from 2020 to 2025. 

The scheme is divided into two components: the Inland Fisheries and the Marine Fisheries. 

The Inland Fisheries component includes the establishment of Medium Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS). 

The establishment of Medium RAS Culture System is particularly significant in states like Gujarat. 

The primary objective of the PMMSY is to increase fish production to 22 million metric tons by 2024-2025. 

This is a substantial increase from the 13.7 million metric tons produced in 2018-2019. 

The scheme aims to achieve this target through various interventions. 

These interventions include the establishment of modern fishing infrastructure. 

They also include the promotion of fish farming and aquaculture practices. 

The benefits of the PMMSY are multifaceted. 

The scheme provides financial assistance to fish farmers. 

Under the PMMSY, fish farmers can receive up to 40% of the project cost as a subsidy. 

For SC/ST and women beneficiaries, this subsidy can go up to 60%. 

The maximum project cost for establishing a Medium RAS is ₹2 crores. 

This means that a SC/ST or women beneficiary can receive a subsidy of ₹1.2 crores. 

The scheme also provides assistance for the construction of fish seed hatcheries. 

Financial support for hatcheries can be up to ₹1 crore. 

The PMMSY also emphasizes skill development and capacity building. 

The scheme aims to train 1.5 million fishers and fish farmers over its duration. 

Eligibility criteria for the PMMSY are specific and clearly defined. 

Beneficiaries must be registered fish farmers or fishers. 

They should be involved in aquaculture or fisheries-related activities. 

The age limit for applicants is generally set at 18 years and above. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required for eligibility. 

However, applicants must demonstrate a commitment to fish farming practices. 

The application process for the PMMSY is straightforward. 

Interested beneficiaries must submit an application to the respective State Fisheries Department. 

The application should include a detailed project report. 

The project report must outline the proposed activities and budget. 

Required documents include identity proof, address proof, and bank account details. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the State Fisheries Department. 

The department may conduct a field verification of the proposed project site. 

Upon approval, the financial assistance will be disbursed. 

The disbursement is typically made in installments based on project milestones. 

The PMMSY has specific timelines for implementation. 

The scheme was launched in 2020 and is set to continue until 2025. 

Regular monitoring and evaluation of the projects are conducted by the implementing agencies. 

The Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying is the nodal ministry for the PMMSY. 

State Fisheries Departments are responsible for the implementation at the state level. 

They coordinate with local bodies and stakeholders to ensure effective execution. 

The PMMSY also aims to promote the use of technology in fisheries. 

This includes the adoption of modern aquaculture practices. 

The scheme encourages the use of biofloc technology and RAS. 

These technologies help in increasing fish production efficiently. 

The PMMSY also focuses on the conservation of aquatic resources. 

It aims to promote sustainable fishing practices. 

This is crucial for maintaining ecological balance in water bodies. 

The scheme also addresses the socio-economic conditions of fishers. 

It aims to enhance their livelihoods and improve their standard of living. 

The PMMSY is expected to create significant employment opportunities. 

It is projected that around 15 million direct and indirect jobs will be generated. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of women in fisheries. 

It encourages their participation in fish farming and related activities. 

The PMMSY aligns with the broader goals of the Government of India. 

It supports the vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The scheme also contributes to the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative. 

This initiative aims to make India self-reliant in various sectors including fisheries. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive approach to revitalize the fisheries sector. 

It aims to ensure food security and nutritional security through increased fish production. 

The scheme is expected to have a transformative impact on the fisheries landscape in India. 

The establishment of Medium RAS Culture Systems in Gujarat is a key component of this transformation. 

This initiative will not only boost fish production but also enhance the livelihoods of local communities. 

The PMMSY is a significant step towards sustainable development in the fisheries sector. 

It is designed to empower fishers and promote responsible fishing practices. 

The successful implementation of the PMMSY will require collaboration among various stakeholders. 

This includes government agencies, local communities, and the private sector. 

The PMMSY is a forward-looking scheme that aims to harness the potential of India's vast aquatic resources. 

It is an essential part of the country's strategy to achieve sustainable economic growth. 

The establishment of Medium RAS Culture Systems is a vital aspect of this strategy. 

Overall, the PMMSY represents a holistic approach to fisheries management and development. 

It is poised to make a lasting impact on the livelihoods of millions of fishers across India.
